title: Why Drains Gurgle and Lose Their Water Seal
description: Gurgling noises in a drainage system often point to venting issues rather than simple clogs. When wastewater travels down an unvented or blocked drain pipe, it creates a partial vacuum behind the flowing column of water. This negative air pressure pulls air through the path of least resistance, which is frequently the water seal inside a nearby P-trap. As air bubbles break through the trap seal, it creates a distinct gurgling sound and depletes the water volume. Without a complete water seal, foul sewer gases can freely enter living spaces. Proper venting balances atmospheric pressure and prevents trap siphoning.
